messages:
Jordan (Acme): Hey team — our CI run is getting a string of 429s during onboarding e2e. Happens only in the first ~30s burst, then things settle.
Maya (CS): ugh, thanks for flagging. which SDK and version are you on? any corporate proxy or special network in front of the runners?
Jordan (Acme): using redwood-js v0.4.2. CI spins up ~40 workers that all call /v1/generate during test init. We have a transparent company proxy that terminates TLS.
Jordan (Acme): here's the client log excerpt:
```
POST /v1/generate -> 429
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1682345123
{"error":"rate limit exceeded"}
```
Sam (Eng): that pattern screams preflight/handshake fanout. If the proxy ends connections or strips headers that let the SDK reuse auth/session state, each worker ends up doing its own handshake -> synchronized token bursts.
Sam (Eng): please paste the raw request headers your CI emits (as seen on the proxy) and confirm if `connection` is keep-alive or close.
Jordan (Acme): proxy shows these headers from the runners:
```
:authority: api.redwood.example
authorization: Bearer <ephemeral-token>
content-type: application/json
connection: close
```
Maya (CS): "connection: close" is the smoking gun. The JS SDK relies on persistent HTTP/TCP/TLS sessions to amortize ephemeral token refreshes and keep a single auth context. If each request closes the session, token refreshes multiply.
Rajat (SRE): adding context: our gateway applies a per-source burst control for new TLS handshakes. Lots of short-lived sessions in a narrow window are treated like many clients — token buckets get exhausted quickly and you see 429s. We've hit this with CI + proxies before.
Sam (Eng): immediate client-side mitigations you can try (no infra changes): reduce concurrency, enable preflight coalescing, and add jittered token refresh. In redwood-js try:
```
Redwood.init({
  concurrency: 3,
  preflightCoalesce: true,
  tokenRefresh: { mode: 'lazy', jitterMs: 250 }
})
```
Sam (Eng): that will limit simultaneous handshakes and spread refreshes so the gateway doesn't see a cliff.
Jordan (Acme): good suggestion. Can the gateway surface any headers our proxy could honor to avoid aggressive connection teardown? Right now the proxy kills idle after N seconds.
Rajat (SRE): gateway already sends x-rate-limit-* and x-redwood-backoff headers. If your proxy preserves and exposes those to the runners it can back off retries. Ultimately, the robust fix is to let the proxy support keepalive (longer idle timeout) so sessions persist across test calls.
Maya (CS): temporary CS playbook: stagger test worker startups (200–500ms gaps) + set SDK concurrency to 3. We'll open an enablement note for your account: "Proxy TLS termination + connection: close -> preflight fanout; recommend keepalive or client concurrency caps."
Jordan (Acme): applying SDK config and staggering CI now. Will report back.
(8 minutes later)
Jordan (Acme): reran 3 times with the config change and staggered starts — initial ramp had no 429s. Nice!
Maya (CS): great. we'll annotate your onboarding record and add an internal KB entry for other accounts with similar proxy setups.
Sam (Eng): follow-up action: we'll add an SDK telemetry check to detect high preflight churn and surface a warning in the console. Filing ENG ticket for redwood-js preflight telemetry.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for redwood-js@v0.4.3-preflight-coalesce
Jordan (Acme): thanks all — will reopen if the problem reappears.
